title: BVOD PG vs. Direct
challenge: Nutra aimed to launch a major branding campaign for their 2025 Afterpay Day sale following a successful 2024 burst.  The challenge was to improve cost-efficiency while maintaining high-quality video placements. They needed to navigate the trade-off between the lower costs of programmatic buying and the reduced granular control over mid-campaign audience optimizations and general changes.
approach: We transitioned from a direct deal used in the previous year to a Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) campaign via The Trade Desk.  This shift allowed us to unlock significantly cheaper CPMs for the brand. By locking in the inventory programmatically, we were able to increase total impressions significantly while only needing a very small budget increase to support the broader reach goals.

title: PMax Brand Exclusion
challenge: After an internal audit, Nutra suggested they were not maximizing PMax visibility on generic terms. The challenge was to prove that excluding brand terms from PMax and moving them to a manual shopping campaign would increase sales on highly competitive generic terms. We had to monitor if this shift would improve overall account efficiency or lead to a drop in total conversions.
approach: We implemented a manual shopping campaign specifically targeting brand terms while simultaneously excluding those same branded searches from the current PMax campaign.  This was designed to force the PMax algorithm to focus exclusively on generic search queries. The goal was to ensure that the AI-driven budget was being spent on new user acquisition rather than capturing existing brand demand.

title: Elevating Brand Presence and Maximising Retail ROI

approach: To maximize reach and potentially lower CPC in our generic search campaigns, we transitioned all phrase match keywords to broad match. We subsequently monitored performance to assess the effectiveness of this strategy.
